problem: The support is defined only through the discrete pmf ('the set of pairs with p(x,y)>0'), and the continuous paragraph never says what the support of a joint pdf is. A student may carry the pmf wording over to the continuous case, where a point with f>0 still has probability 0.
fix: Add: 'For continuous variables the support is the region where f(x,y)>0 (more precisely its closure); points outside it have density 0.'

where: Section 2, sentence on limits of the CDF
problem: 'tends to 0 at either -∞' is compressed and can be misread. F is a function of two variables; the two one-variable limits need to be stated separately.
fix: Write: 'lim(x→-∞) F(x,y)=0 for every fixed y, lim(y→-∞) F(x,y)=0 for every fixed x, and lim(x,y)→(+∞,+∞) F(x,y)=1.'

where: Section 3, bullet 3 ('If J=0 at a point, treat that point separately')
problem: The real condition for the change-of-variables formula is that the map be one-to-one on the region. A vanishing Jacobian means the map is not locally invertible there, so the formula does not apply at that point. Saying 'treat that point separately' is vague and could suggest that a single point where J=0 can be patched up without checking one-to-one-ness.
fix: 'If J=0 on a set, the map is not locally one-to-one there; split the region so that the map is one-to-one on each piece, then add the pieces. A set of zero area (e.g. one point or one curve) does not change the total probability, but the formula still must be applied only where the map is one-to-one.'

where: Lead, last sentence before the sections
problem: It says the joint pmf, pdf 'or joint CDF' lets you compute P((X,Y)∈A). For the CDF this is only practical for orthants and rectangles; for a general region A the pmf or pdf (double sum/integral) is what you use.
fix: 'The joint pmf or joint pdf lets you compute P((X,Y)∈A) directly by a double sum or double integral, and the joint CDF gives such probabilities for rectangles and orthants.'

problem: Step 3 suddenly computes p(0,0) with no link to the question. The reader has to work out that this is the preparation for part (b).
fix: Open the step with 'For part (b) we first need p(0,0):' and then keep the existing count.
